result.report:
PASS for the specified-tree conditional theorem, including the stronger construction on the entire actual interior Ω and uniform decreasing convergence on all of Z. This does not establish original P06.2 or its all-curve gate. The supplied model, tree, retraction and harmonic factorization are hypotheses; they are not conclusions inferred from a current equation.

I checked the main proof and its supporting constructions independently. The relevant Thuillier and Berkovich primary proof bodies supplied in the question were checked directly; browser retrieval of those archival PDFs was blocked. Accessible primary bodies were opened for the other foundations and for clarification of the formal étale application. Compilation, hashes, prior verdicts and the draft’s status labels played no mathematical role.

The algebraic preliminaries justify the global-fraction lift. Rig-smoothness gives regularity; connectedness then leaves one integral component. A nonzero global analytic function consequently has only finitely many rigid zeros. A model vertex has zero kernel, so Frac(O(Z)) is dense in H(v). Approximating a norm-one lift within distance less than one preserves its reduction exactly. The resulting numerator and denominator introduce only finitely many exceptional directions.

The formal-chart argument applies in every characteristic and does not require a discrete valuation or a Noetherian valuation ring. One can use a principal ideal of definition (c), with 0<|c|<1. The formal étale criterion, local standard étale presentations and uniqueness over nilpotent thickenings justify the stated local Jacobian presentation. On each strict closed subdomain the initial error has norm q<1, the Jacobian inverse has norm at most one, and Newton errors are bounded by q^(2^j). The Taylor estimate uses no factorial division. Uniqueness also holds after evaluation in completed residue fields. Thus the argument identifies the whole selected ordinary tube, including nonrigid points, and not merely its rigid points.

The tree calculation is correct: child-subtree masses give outgoing sum μ at every vertex, including the root. Rational slope rounding integrates consistently because there are no cycles. The uniform error is at most Lη₀ and the vertex-sum error at most dη₀. The chosen strict margins therefore establish the positive outgoing sums needed for every residual construction. The point-skeleton and empty-interior-vertex cases are covered separately.

The residual movement lemma works with signed coefficients q_i. With deg E≥max(1,2g), both K−E and K−E+p have negative degree, so ℓ(E)−ℓ(E−p)=1. Avoiding finitely many proper evaluation kernels gives exact prescribed orders, rather than order inequalities. The additional divisor is effective, avoids every forbidden point, and has degree NΣq_i. Proper interior residual components meet the projective hypothesis. No degree-zero principality or genus restriction is assumed.

The star lemma establishes one actual unit on one common ordinary open neighborhood. Its finite inner-disc removals are compact and closed, and its graph arms avoid all remaining retracted zeros and poles. For each slope computation the refined formal open retains the selected node and both component generic points, removes the other nodes and reductions of zeros and poles, and makes the quotient a unit on the entire generic fibre. This establishes the one-node antecedent of Thuillier’s slope lemma at every application. The sign is correct: the outgoing slope of log|f| is minus the residual order. Unit restrictions to full annular collars give exact affine values on every fibre. In all remaining residue discs, the maximum principles for f and f⁻¹ force constant modulus. Zero-order lift exceptions are handled by their exact constant collars, without asserting units farther inside those exceptional discs.

The cap construction is valid. Its annulus excludes the vertex, its overlap with the central star is a whole ordinary open collar, and its overlap with the inner disc lies entirely on the new plateau c−ar. The strict inequalities leave room for both overlaps and give a uniform error smaller than ε. It never restores the old constant c. The finitely many stars, edge annuli, caps and disc continuations cover Ω and agree exactly on ordinary open overlaps. Full edge fibres, attached discs and type-3 and type-4 points are included. The replacement regions stay away from B, so the glued function extends continuously to Z and equals G∘τ near B.

Ordinary smoothness follows from actual analytic-unit moments. The Hessian vanishes in central stars, edge annuli and constant regions; a cap contributes q''(t)d't∧d''t with q''≥0. In any refined test chart its contribution is mαφq''(t)Aα²dξ≥0 with the actual positive calibration mα. Collapsed directions contribute zero, and inseparable degrees are retained. Exact smooth overlaps create no interface distributions. Canonical integration and boundaryless Green’s formula therefore prove positivity against every compact nonnegative ordinary test. No psh partition gluing or weak-smoothness substitution occurs.

Finally, c_n=(5/3)b_n satisfies c_n−c_(n+1)=b_n+b_(n+1). The error bounds give decreasing approximants from above with error at most (8/3)b_n. Both signs and every stage use the entire same Z and the same ordinary neighborhood Ω. Restriction proves the assertion on precisely the supplied Y.

Harmless corrections: Hartshorne’s canonical-degree statement is IV, Example 1.3.3, rather than the cited Corollary 1.4; the open projective completion statement is I, Corollary 6.10, following Theorem 6.9. Where the supplied source describes a normalized residual function as independent of the normalizing scalar, its divisor and orders are independent; the function itself can change by a nonzero residue-field scalar. None of these corrections changes the construction. No substantial repair or indispensable unsettled mathematical step remains.

For a compact rig-smooth strict curve with a simply semistable formal model, skeletal vertices correspond to special-fibre components and edges to nodes. Boundary vertices correspond to nonproper components. A node p has edge weight [κ(p):k̃], and a local node equation XY=a gives edge length −log|a|; the skeletal retraction is compatible with formal étale charts. Thuillier, Theorem 2.2.10 and §2.2.3; Gubler–Jell–Rabinoff, §15.2.

For a simply semistable formal curve over an algebraically closed complete field C, a model vertex v is type 2, its residual function field is the function field of its special-fibre component, and |H(v)×|=|C×|. Reduction fibres away from model vertices correspond to closed special-fibre points; nodes give graph directions and smooth closed points give the remaining residue directions. Thuillier, Proposition 2.1.2, Lemma 2.1.13 and §2.2.2–2.2.3.

For adic formal schemes of finite ideal type, an adic morphism is étale exactly when all its reductions modulo powers of a finitely generated ideal of definition are étale. Étale ring maps are locally standard étale, and reduction modulo a nilpotent ideal induces an equivalence of étale-algebra categories. Consequently a topologically finitely presented étale formal chart admits locally a finite equation presentation with invertible square Jacobian and localizing denominators nonzero at the selected residual point. Fujiwara–Kato, Foundations of Rigid Geometry I, Proposition I.5.3.11; EGA IV, §17; Stacks Project, Tags 00UE and 0ALI.

passages.statement: For a smooth projective connected curve R of genus g over an algebraically closed field and any divisor D, ℓ(D)−ℓ(K_R−D)=deg D+1−g and deg K_R=2g−2. Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry, IV, Theorem 1.3 and Example 1.3.3.

For a simply semistable formal curve with generic fibre X and a global analytic function f generically invertible on X, its skeletal logarithm F is integral piecewise affine; log|f|≤F(x) on each retraction fibre over x, with equality on the whole fibre exactly when f has no zero there. At an interior skeletal point, the outgoing weighted slope sum equals the degree of the zero divisor on that fibre. In particular, a unit on a standard closed annulus has an affine logarithm equal to that affine value on every whole retraction fibre. Thuillier, Proposition 2.2.24 and Lemma 2.2.1.

For a connected simply semistable formal curve whose special fibre has exactly one node p, and an analytic unit f on its entire generic fibre, the outgoing slope of log|f| at a component vertex v is −ord_p(f̃_v), after normalizing |f(v)| to one. The residual divisor and its orders are independent of the normalizing scalar. Thuillier, Lemma 2.2.25.

A finite set of type-2 cuts in a simply semistable curve can be realized as vertices after a finite separable ground-field extension and an admissible blowup with simply semistable result. Over an algebraically closed ground field the extension is trivial. For such a blowup, the original skeleton embeds in the refined skeleton and the original retraction is the composition of the refined retraction with the skeletal collapse. Thuillier, Lemma 2.2.22 and Proposition 2.2.26(i)–(ii).

On a Hausdorff analytic space, ordinary CLD-smooth functions locally admit expressions as smooth real functions of logarithms of finitely many actual analytic units on ordinary open neighborhoods. Such unit-moment pullbacks are ordinary smooth, and pullback commutes with d′ and d′′. Chambert-Loir–Ducros, Proposition 15.1.1(b), Corollary 15.1.2 and the differential-form pullback construction.

A Hausdorff pure-dimensional analytic space carries the canonical calibrated CLD tropical structure, and its analytic interior is harmonious. The canonical cell calibrations retain the actual positive analytic degrees, including inseparable degrees. Chambert-Loir–Ducros, Theorems 15.6.1 and 15.7.1 and the canonical calibration construction.

On a boundaryless canonically calibrated CLD analytic space of pure dimension one, a smooth function g and a compactly supported smooth scalar test φ satisfy ∫g d′d′′φ=∫φ d′d′′g. Positive smooth top-degree forms integrate nonnegatively. A smooth locally integrable function is psh exactly when its d′d′′ current is positive. Chambert-Loir–Ducros, Proposition 5.11.1, §7.3.1–7.3.4 and Proposition 8.3.1(b).
